SH.tools:
The hackathon provides access to Apheris, Nebius and JapanFold. Check the latest details with the organizers, including which models are enabled.
 JapanFoldStructure prediction and binder-design workbench. Open JapanFold (https://japanfold.aiand.com/).
 NebiusModel catalog and related model services. Browse models (https://forge.nebius.cloud/models/).
 Apheris FoundryAccess is planned for the hackathon. It includes models further optimized using pharmaceutical companies’ proprietary data.
 AMASSScientific intelligence for literature search and verification. You can see the “How to use AMASS” section and try it.
 These tools have agent integrations, and Claude Max credits will be provided, so your agents can do the work and mix and match them while you make decisions.
 Prizes: Apheris and Openfold are the monetary prize sponsors; to qualify for that prize, include Apheris’ version of Openfold in your pipeline. AMASS will award 100 USD in credits to the team with the most creative use of AMASS.
SH.judging:
Schedule, rules and practical details: Everything about the day itself is on the event website: AI × Antibodies Hackathon · Oslo
 Among the different scoring categories, Judgment carries the most weight: we want to know why you made each choice, not only what you built. These weights are provisional and will be confirmed in the final hackathon instructions.
 judging() 
 Each group needs to provide score tables and report where each score came from.
 Judges and mentors
 judgeCards() 
 More judges and mentors coming soon.
 Prizes are sponsored by Apheris, OpenFold and Amass. Adaptyv will test selected designs experimentally (VHHs, Fabs and scFvs, not whole antibodies).
SH.workflow:
Design works like a funnel: you start with many candidates and narrow them down to a few. In the hackathon you do steps 1 to 3, and end with up to 10 designs to present. Step 4 is not part of your work: after you submit your selection, Adaptyv helps test selected designs in the lab.
 funnel([
 ['Generate','VHH, scFv or Fab candidate sequences or structures, either by changing an existing binder or designing a new one from scratch. Usually people generate hundreds or more.','100s+','candidates','You do this',false,100,80],
 ['Score','Candidates are scored with structure-, interface-, affinity- or physics-related tools/ML models, to pick designs that will likely have desirable properties.','ranked','weakest drop out','You do this',false,80,56],
 ['Filter','Choose which candidates to test, judging them on more than affinity or one score. Here, developability becomes an important filtering step. Select up to 10 to validate after the hackathon. You might make them very similar to each other or very different.','≤ 10','to validate','You do this',false,56,32],
 ['Test','The selected designs are tested experimentally by Adaptyv, not by you. We can probably test five designs per team.','~5','tested','Adaptyv, afterwards',true,32,22]
 ]) 
 Every step throws candidates away, so start wide.
 Computational scores help decide what to test, but they do not establish that a candidate binds. A useful workflow combines model predictions, interface scores and developability checks.
 In the hackathon you can explore different ways of generating and ranking designs. Record your inputs, model versions and the reasons for selecting each candidate.
 Why you cannot brute-force itA single CDR3 of 15 residues has 2015 possibilities, about sci(3,19) . Nature searches that space with billions of cells over rounds of mutation and selection. You get one day, and scoring functions correlate with reality far less well than anyone would like.
